title: The Unwritten Contract of Cloud-based Elastic Solid-State Drives
problem: Despite widespread cloud adoption, the performance characteristics and suitability of Elastic SSDs (ESSDs) as local SSD replacements remain uncharacterized, leaving cloud storage users uncertain about deployment decisions.
motivation: As workloads migrate to cloud, users need empirical understanding of ESSD performance contracts and trade-offs vs. local SSDs to optimize storage architecture decisions.
method: Characterizes two production ESSDs from AWS and Alibaba Cloud through comprehensive benchmarking, identifies counter-intuitive performance patterns, and derives design implications for cloud software optimization to exploit ESSD-specific characteristics.
key_novelty: First comprehensive characterization of ESSD performance contracts revealing counter-intuitive behavior patterns that diverge from local SSD expectations.
contributions: Empirical characterization of AWS and Alibaba Cloud ESSDs performance
Four key observations about ESSD behavior contradicting conventional local SSD assumptions
Five design implications for cloud software to exploit ESSD characteristics
Framework for understanding storage-compute disaggregated architecture performance trade-offs
limitations: Not discussed; work is exploratory characterization.
primary_theme: Cloud ESSD performance characterization and design implications
